note: NECO English Paper III objective (lexis and structure) plus Paper IV Test of Orals: fresh items written for NECO candidates, near-duplicate scanned against the JAMB and WAEC banks. Orals items carry the 'Test of Orals —' topic prefix so the Paper IV mock filters them automatically.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The headmaster LAUDDED the students who returned the missing wallet.
questions.explanation: To laud somebody is to commend or praise them publicly.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Judgment was delayed because the evidence was AMBIGUOUS.
questions.explanation: Ambiguous evidence can be read in more than one way, so it is unclear.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The villager's TENUOUS hold on the rope worried the rescuers.
questions.explanation: Tenuous means thin or weak, barely adequate for the purpose.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The nurse was COMMENDED for her quick action during the emergency.
questions.explanation: To commend is to express approval, so she was praised.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Rain ABATED after three days of continuous downpour in Lokoja.
questions.explanation: When rain abates it becomes less severe; it subsides.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The new commissioner's speech was deliberately EVASIVE.
questions.explanation: An evasive speaker avoids giving a direct answer to the question.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The old man NARRATED the story of the civil war to the children.
questions.explanation: To narrate is to tell a story in speech.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The minister's remark was regarded as a GAFFE by the newspapers.
questions.explanation: A gaffe is an unintentional blunder, especially a public one.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Traffic on the bridge was HORRENDOUS during the Friday rush.
questions.explanation: Horrendous means causing horror; extremely bad or dreadful.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The manager tried to APPEASE the angry customers with refunds.
questions.explanation: To appease is to pacify or placate somebody who is angry.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The company recorded a HUGE profit in the last quarter.
questions.explanation: Huge and enormous are close in meaning: extremely large.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The judge described the witness's account as CREDIBLE.
questions.explanation: Credible testimony is believable; it can be accepted as true.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The suspect gave a CONCOCTED alibi to the police.
questions.explanation: A concocted story is fabricated or invented to deceive.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Efforts to curb smuggling have been FUTILE so far.
questions.explanation: Futile effort produces no result; it is unsuccessful.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word GENUINE is the opposite of
questions.explanation: Genuine means real or authentic, so its opposite is fake.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word ABUNDANT is the opposite of
questions.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantity; scarce means insufficient.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word TRANSPARENT is the opposite of
questions.explanation: A transparent object lets light through; an opaque one does not.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word FRUGAL is the opposite of
questions.explanation: A frugal person spends sparingly; a wasteful one squanders.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word BENEFICIAL is the opposite of
questions.explanation: What is beneficial does good; what is harmful does damage.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word SCARCE is the opposite of
questions.explanation: Scarce goods are hard to find; plentiful ones exist in abundance.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word METICULOUS is the opposite of
questions.explanation: A meticulous worker is careful over detail; a careless one is not.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word VOLUNTARY is the opposite of
questions.explanation: A voluntary act is done of one's own will; a compulsory one is forced.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word TEMPORARY is the opposite of
questions.explanation: Temporary work lasts a short time; permanent work lasts long.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word VICTORY is the opposite of
questions.explanation: Victory is the opposite of defeat in a contest.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word ARTIFICIAL is the opposite of
questions.explanation: Artificial things are made by people; natural things occur by nature.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The word LENIENT is the opposite of
questions.explanation: A lenient teacher punishes lightly; a strict one insists on rules.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: When the chairman said the matter was 'a storm in a teacup', he meant it was
questions.D: a fuss over a small matter
questions.explanation: A storm in a teacup is great excitement or anger about something trivial.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Ada 'burned the midnight oil' before her NECO examinations. This means she
questions.explanation: To burn the midnight oil is to work or study far into the night.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: To 'let the cat out of the bag' is to
questions.explanation: The idiom means to disclose a secret, usually by accident.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The governor's promise was described as 'a pie in the sky'. This means it was
questions.explanation: A pie in the sky is a benefit that is unlikely ever to materialise.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Emeka 'took the bull by the horns' when he
questions.explanation: Taking the bull by the horns means confronting a problem directly and boldly.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: A person who 'plays second fiddle' is one who
questions.explanation: To play second fiddle is to take a less important position than somebody else.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The treasurer was told to 'keep the books' of the association. This means to
questions.explanation: Keeping the books means maintaining the accounts of an organisation.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: When the villagers said the flood 'broke the camel's back', they meant it
questions.explanation: The straw that broke the camel's back is the last small burden that makes everything collapse.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: To be 'at the mercy of' the weather is to be
questions.explanation: Being at the mercy of something means being helpless against it.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The youth leader 'poured cold water' on the proposal. He
questions.explanation: To pour cold water on an idea is to discourage or criticise it.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: 'Once in a blue moon' means
questions.explanation: A blue moon is a rare event, so the phrase means very seldom.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The manager said the new worker was 'a square peg in a round hole'. The worker was
questions.explanation: A square peg in a round hole is somebody placed in a job that does not suit them.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The traveller had to ___ a heavy toll on the new expressway.
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'pay a toll', not give or make.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The insurgents agreed to ___ arms after the peace talks.
questions.explanation: To surrender weapons is to 'lay down arms'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The panel will ___ a decision on the dispute next week.
questions.explanation: One reaches a decision; 'arrive' would need 'at a decision'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The suspect was asked to ___ an oath on the holy book.
questions.explanation: The legal collocation is 'take an oath'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Bola ___ a first class degree in Economics last year.
questions.explanation: One earns a degree through study; 'won' belongs with prizes.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Villagers were advised to ___ shelter before the storm arrived.
questions.explanation: The usual collocation is 'take shelter'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The chairman ___ the meeting to order at exactly ten o'clock.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'call the meeting to order'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The state government ___ a curfew on the restive town.
questions.explanation: A curfew is 'imposed'; enforcement follows later.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: It is rude to ___ fun of a person's disability.
questions.explanation: The idiom is 'make fun of' somebody.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The doctor told the patient to ___ a rest from work.
questions.explanation: 'Have a rest' is standard; the others are not natural English.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The chief entered in his FULL regalia. The word 'full' here suggests
questions.explanation: Full regalia means the complete set of ceremonial garments.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The pupils are well GROUNDED in mathematics. This means they have
questions.explanation: To be grounded in a subject is to have a firm foundation in it.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The lawyer withdrew from the case on HEALTH grounds. 'Health' here refers to
questions.explanation: Withdrawing on health grounds means because of one's medical condition.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The manager's reply was a diplomatic WAY OUT of the argument. This means the reply
questions.explanation: A way out is an escape route from a difficulty.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The essay was MARKED DOWN for poor paragraphing. The student lost marks because
questions.explanation: Marked down means having marks deducted for a stated fault.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Their victory was NARROW. The margin of victory was
questions.explanation: A narrow win is one achieved by a small margin.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The judge threw the case OUT for lack of evidence. The case was
questions.explanation: To throw out a case is to dismiss it.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The contractor did a RUNNING job on the roof. The work was
questions.explanation: A 'running job' is colloquial for shoddy, hurried work.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The girl takes after her mother in LOOKS. 'Looks' here means
questions.explanation: Looks refers to a person's appearance, not behaviour.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The senator's support gave the bill TEETH. The bill became
questions.explanation: Giving a law teeth means giving it the power to be enforced.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: By the time the firefighters arrived, the warehouse ___ for an hour.
questions.explanation: The earlier of two past events takes the past perfect: had been burning.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Ngozi ___ her assignment before she watched the news.
questions.explanation: The action completed first takes the past perfect 'had finished'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The engineers ___ the bridge since January, and it is still under repair.
questions.explanation: An action that began in the past and continues needs the present perfect continuous.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius.
questions.explanation: Scientific truths are stated in the simple present tense.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: When I called at noon, the family ___ lunch.
questions.explanation: An action in progress at a past moment takes the past continuous.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Next session, my sister ___ Economics at the university.
questions.explanation: A future plan takes the simple future 'will study'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The refugees ___ in the camp for two months before aid arrived.
questions.explanation: Duration before a past reference point requires the past perfect.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Look! The flag ___ in the wind.
questions.explanation: An action happening now, with 'look', takes the present continuous.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: My grandfather ___ to the village every December.
questions.explanation: A habitual action takes the simple present, and the subject is singular.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: If the alarm had rung earlier, the workers ___ the building in time.
questions.explanation: A third conditional pairs 'had + participle' with 'would have + participle'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The principal ___ the assembly when the lights went out.
questions.explanation: The interrupted past action takes the past continuous.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Tunde ___ in Kano for five years, but he lives in Enugu now.
questions.explanation: A finished period in the past takes the simple past 'lived'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Each of the candidates ___ a pen and a ruler.
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so the verb takes the singular form.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ the answer.
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor' the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The news of the victories ___ the whole town.
questions.explanation: 'News' is singular despite its plural-looking form.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Mathematics ___ the subject Ada dislikes most.
questions.explanation: School subjects like mathematics are treated as singular.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The number of applicants this year ___ surprising.
questions.explanation: 'The number of' takes a singular verb; 'a number of' would take plural.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Bread and butter ___ my usual breakfast.
questions.explanation: Bread and butter is one combined item, so it takes a singular verb.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: One of the boys ___ the window during the match.
questions.explanation: The real subject is 'one', which is singular.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Everybody in the two villages ___ the new borehole.
questions.explanation: 'Everybody' is always singular.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The police ___ investigating the robbery.
questions.explanation: 'Police' is a plural noun in English and takes a plural verb.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: A series of lectures ___ been arranged for the fresh students.
questions.explanation: 'A series of' is treated as a single unit and takes the singular.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The suspect was charged ___ arson.
questions.explanation: The correct collocation is 'charged with' an offence.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Halima is interested ___ poultry farming.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'interested in' something.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The council blamed the flooding ___ blocked drainages.
questions.explanation: You blame something ON a cause, or blame a person FOR an offence.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The retired headmaster now lives ___ a small pension.
questions.explanation: To live on a pension means to depend on it for survival.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: We congratulated the team ___ their victory.
questions.explanation: Congratulate somebody ON an achievement.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The patient is responding ___ treatment very well.
questions.explanation: The fixed expression is 'respond to treatment'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The two rival groups agreed ___ a ceasefire.
questions.explanation: Parties agree ON terms; a person agrees WITH another person.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Auntie Ngozi is married ___ a lawyer from Enugu.
questions.explanation: The standard collocation is 'married to' somebody.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The lecturer insisted ___ seeing the Dean immediately.
questions.explanation: Insist always takes 'on' before the gerund.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The auditor was accused ___ negligence ___ duty.
questions.explanation: One is accused OF an offence committed IN the course of duty.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The harvest failed; ___, the family managed to eat.
questions.explanation: A contrast between two clauses is signalled by 'nevertheless'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ___ he had no money, he could not travel home.
questions.explanation: 'Since' introduces the reason for the second clause.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The play was long; ___, the audience stayed to the end.
questions.explanation: 'However' signals a contrast with what might have been expected.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: You will not pass the examination ___ you revise thoroughly.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not', which fits the condition here.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Ada studied hard, ___ she passed her NECO examination.
questions.explanation: The second clause is a result, so 'therefore' links them.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The teacher was strict ___ kind to the younger pupils.
questions.explanation: The two adjectives contrast, requiring 'but'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ___ the heavy rain, the match went ahead as planned.
questions.explanation: 'Despite' takes a noun phrase directly, without 'of'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The bank manager, ___ was recently promoted, has resigned.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative pronoun for a person.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: There isn't ___ water left in the drum.
questions.explanation: 'Water' is uncountable, so it takes 'much', not 'many'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ___ of the two roads leads to the market.
questions.explanation: For a choice between two, 'either' means one or the other.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The twins look alike; I cannot tell one from ___.
questions.explanation: Of a pair, the second is 'the other'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: ___ student must bring ___ own calculator.
questions.explanation: 'Every' is singular and takes a singular possessive.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: I have ___ interest in politics whatsoever.
questions.explanation: 'Interest' is uncountable and the sense is negative, so 'little'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: It was ___ who rescued the drowning boy.
questions.explanation: After 'it was', the subject pronoun 'he' is required in formal English.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: The woman ___ car was stolen reported to the police.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession before the noun 'car'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Between you and ___, the plan will fail.
questions.explanation: After the preposition 'between', the object pronoun 'me' is correct.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word contains the same vowel sound as in 'seat'?
questions.explanation: 'Seat' and 'chief' both have the long vowel /iː/; 'sit' has the short /ɪ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which of these words is the vowel /e/ pronounced?
questions.explanation: 'Bread' rhymes with 'bed', giving the short vowel /e/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word contains the vowel /ɑː/ as in 'father'?
questions.explanation: 'Laugh' ends with the long /ɑː/, as in 'father'; the others have short vowels.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word contains the diphthong /ɔɪ/ as in 'coin'?
questions.explanation: 'Noise' shares the /ɔɪ/ diphthong with 'coin'.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word contains the same vowel sound as in 'food'?
questions.explanation: 'Truth' has /uː/ like 'food'; 'good' has /ʊ/ and 'blood' has /ʌ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word does 'oo' represent the short vowel /ʊ/?
questions.explanation: In 'wool', 'oo' is the short /ʊ/, unlike the long /uː/ in 'moon'.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word contains the diphthong /aʊ/ as in 'house'?
questions.explanation: 'Cloud' shares the /aʊ/ sound with 'house'.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word contains the vowel /ʌ/ as in 'cut'?
questions.explanation: 'Young' has the /ʌ/ sound, like 'cut'.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word contains the diphthong /eɪ/ as in 'day'?
questions.explanation: 'Weight' shares the /eɪ/ diphthong with 'day'; 'height' has /aɪ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word does the letter 'a' represent the weak vowel /ə/?
questions.explanation: In 'along', the first 'a' is the unstressed schwa /ə/; the others carry full vowels.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word contains the diphthong /əʊ/ as in 'go'?
questions.explanation: 'Soul' rhymes with 'go', sharing the /əʊ/ diphthong.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word contains the same vowel sound as in 'ear'?
questions.explanation: 'Ear' and 'idea' share the /ɪə/ sound; 'era' has /ɪərə/ but 'idea' is closest with /ɪə/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word does the letter 'a' represent /ɔː/?
questions.explanation: Before 'll', the letter 'a' is pronounced /ɔː/, as in 'ball'.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word contains the diphthong /eə/ as in 'hair'?
questions.explanation: 'Stare' shares the /eə/ diphthong with 'hair'.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: Which word has the same vowel sound as in 'work'?
questions.explanation: 'Work' and 'hurt' both carry the /ɜː/ vowel.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Vowels and Diphthongs
questions.q: In which word are the letters 'ui' pronounced /uː/?
questions.explanation: In 'fruit', 'ui' gives the long /uː/; in 'build', 'guilt' and 'quick' it is short /ɪ/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'p' silent?
questions.explanation: In 'pneumonia', the initial 'pn' is pronounced /n/, so the 'p' is silent.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: Which word ends with the voiceless consonant /s/?
questions.explanation: After the voiceless /t/, the plural ending is /s/ as in 'cats'.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word does 'ch' represent /k/?
questions.explanation: In words of Greek origin like 'school', 'ch' is pronounced /k/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: Which word contains the consonant /ʒ/ as in 'vision'?
questions.explanation: 'Measure' has the /ʒ/ sound in its middle, like 'vision'.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is the /θ/ sound as in 'think' heard?
questions.explanation: 'Author' begins its second syllable with the voiceless /θ/; the others have /ð/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: Which word begins with the consonant cluster /st/?
questions.explanation: 'Strip' begins with the three-consonant cluster /str/, which contains /st/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word is the final consonant /d/ pronounced?
questions.explanation: After the voiced /b/, the past ending is /d/, as in 'robbed'.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: In which word does 'gh' represent /f/?
questions.explanation: In 'tough', 'gh' is /f/; in 'though' and 'through' it is silent.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: Which word contains the silent letter 'b'?
questions.explanation: The 'b' in 'doubt' is silent; it is pronounced in 'cabin' and 'rabbit'.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Consonants and Clusters
questions.q: Which word ends with the voiced consonant /z/?
questions.explanation: After the voiced /d/, the plural ending is /z/, as in 'floods'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'night'?
questions.explanation: 'Night' and 'height' share the ending sound /aɪt/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'bread'?
questions.explanation: 'Bread' and 'spread' both end with the /ed/ sound pronounced /ɛd/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'laugh'?
questions.explanation: 'Laugh' /lɑːf/ rhymes with 'staff' /stɑːf/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'coin'?
questions.explanation: 'Coin' and 'join' share the diphthong ending /ɔɪn/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'wealth'?
questions.explanation: 'Wealth' and 'health' end with the same /ɛlθ/ sound.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'rough'?
questions.explanation: 'Rough' /rʌf/ rhymes with 'stuff' /stʌf/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'colonel'?
questions.explanation: 'Colonel' is pronounced /ˈkɜːnl/, rhyming with 'journal' /ˈdʒɜːnl/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which word rhymes with 'plague'?
questions.explanation: 'Plague' /pleɪɡ/ rhymes with 'vague' /veɪɡ/; 'league' has /iː/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which of these words is stressed on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: 'MARket' carries its stress on the first syllable; the others stress the second.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which of these words is stressed on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: In 'arREST' (verb or noun), the second syllable takes the stress.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which word is stressed on the THIRD syllable?
questions.explanation: In 'deveLOPment', the third syllable carries the main stress.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In which of these words is the stress on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: In 'eduCAtion', the second syllable 'ca' takes the primary stress.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In which word is the stress on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: 'TEACHer' is stressed on the first syllable, unlike the verb-like words listed.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In which word is the stress placed on the THIRD syllable?
questions.explanation: In 'underSTANDing', the third syllable carries the primary stress.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In which of these words does the stress fall on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: In 'hoTEL', a French loan word, the second syllable is stressed.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In which of these words does the stress fall on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: 'COMfortable' is stressed on its first syllable; the others stress later syllables.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In which word is the stress on the THIRD syllable?
questions.explanation: In 'agriCULture', the main stress falls on the third syllable.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which of these two-syllable words is stressed on the SECOND syllable?
questions.explanation: Both 'canal' and 'canteen' take second-syllable stress; 'canAL' is the standard example.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which word is stressed on the FIRST syllable?
questions.explanation: 'BASKet' has first-syllable stress; the prepositions listed stress the second.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Pick the word whose stress falls on the SECOND syllable.
questions.explanation: In 'preVENtion', the second syllable carries the stress, as in 'prevent'.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: A question expecting the answer 'yes' or 'no' usually ends with a
questions.explanation: Yes/no questions normally end on a rising tone.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Statements in English normally end with a
questions.explanation: A completed statement takes a falling tone.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: 'Where did you keep the file?' The question ends with a
questions.explanation: Wh-questions, asking for information, end with a falling tone.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In the list 'beans, rice, yams and plantains', the word 'plantains' is said with a
questions.A: falling tone, marking the end of the list
questions.B: rising tone like the earlier items
questions.explanation: Non-final list items rise, while the final item falls to close the list.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: A polite request such as 'Could you open the window?' often ends with a
questions.explanation: Requests framed as yes/no questions keep the rising tone.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: A command such as 'Shut the door!' is normally said with a
questions.explanation: Commands, like statements, are completed with a falling tone.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: In 'You PASSED?' expressing surprise, the speaker's voice
questions.explanation: A declarative question used to show surprise carries a rising tone.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which pair of words are homophones?
questions.explanation: 'Sight' and 'site' are both pronounced /saɪt/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which pair contains words that sound the SAME?
questions.explanation: 'Aloud' and 'allowed' are both pronounced /əˈlaʊd/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which pair of words is pronounced identically?
questions.explanation: 'Peace' and 'piece' share the pronunciation /piːs/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which of these is a homophone of 'flour'?
questions.explanation: 'Flour' and 'flower' are both pronounced /ˈflaʊə/.

questions.subject: English
questions.q: Which of these pairs consists of homophones?
questions.explanation: 'Whine' and 'wine' are both pronounced /waɪn/ in present-day English.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'k' silent?
questions.explanation: In 'know', the 'k' before 'n' at the start of the word is silent.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word does the letter 'c' represent /s/?
questions.explanation: Before 'i', the soft 'c' of 'city' is pronounced /s/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'h' silent?
questions.explanation: The 'h' of 'honour' is silent; the word begins with a vowel sound.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word does 'tion' NOT sound like /ʃən/?
questions.explanation: In 'question', the 'tion' is part of /tʃən/, unlike the usual /ʃən/.

questions.subject: English
questions.topic: Test of Orals — Letters and Letter Groups
questions.q: In which word is the letter 'g' pronounced /dʒ/?
questions.explanation: Before 'e', the 'g' of 'gem' is soft, pronounced /dʒ/.
